camera.position: chest level just behind and beside Nora's right shoulder, looking past her toward a small fern clearing
camera.framing: Nora's shoulder, ponytail and three-quarter profile fill the right third of the foreground; one juvenile Triceratops stands in the left two thirds of the frame in the midground, about two meters beyond the mossy log; tall conifer trunks and morning haze behind

setting.location: Hell Creek floodplain forest, Montana, Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago, warm humid morning
elements: soft hazy morning sunlight slants in from the upper left between tall straight conifer trunks; the air is warm and humid with a light haze; no snow, no frost, no winter anywhere
the ground is damp dark soil covered with low ankle-high ferns; there is no grass lawn
one fallen moss-covered log lies across the right foreground from frame 0; it stays in that same spot for the whole clip
one dense waist-high clump of tall green fern fronds stands in the left midground from frame 0; its fronds stay rooted in place and only sway when the animal brushes past them

exactly one juvenile Triceratops is already standing behind the fern clump from frame 0: its head, frill and front half are visible above and between the fronds, its hind half hidden behind them; it stays the only animal in the whole clip, it never appears suddenly and never vanishes

the juvenile Triceratops is about as tall as a pony at the shoulder, with a heavy rounded body on four thick legs, pebbly olive-brown scaly skin with darker mottling, a short hooked parrot-like beak, one short nose horn, two short brow horns that curve slightly backward, and a bony neck frill with a scalloped edge; it is a dinosaur, never a rhinoceros, never a cow, never a lizard, with no fur and no feathers

characters.name: Nora
characters.visual_lock: matches Nora face and Nora Body reference images exactly
characters.outfit: wears the exact historical outfit shown in the Nora Body reference sheet: golden-tan deer suede tunic, dark corset belt, high blonde ponytail (NO shearling collar, NO extra fur, NO hood, NO fringe, NO tassels, NO outfit variations; long tunic sleeves that reach all the way to her wrists, never sleeveless; wide dark belt, tan suede leggings that cover her legs completely from hips to boots, and criss-cross laced knee boots exactly as in the Nora Body reference; no bare skin on her thighs, knees or shins at any moment, even when she kneels)
characters.action: kneels low behind the mossy log, turning her face toward the lens in three-quarter profile while she talks in a hushed, excited voice; for the whole clip her right knee stays pressed into the damp soil, her left boot stays planted flat on the ground, and her left forearm stays resting along the top of the log with the empty left hand lying open on the moss

characters.name: Juvenile Triceratops
characters.visual_lock: described in setting; one animal only
characters.position: standing behind the fern clump in the left midground, about two meters beyond the log, head raised and turned toward Nora; alive for the whole clip: flanks rise and fall with slow breathing, nostrils flare, it blinks, its tail sways slowly, its head tilts a little toward each sound; never frozen like a statue

timeline_action.0-3s: From frame 0 the Triceratops stands still behind the fern clump with its head raised and its beak closed, not eating yet, and every fern frond in front of it is intact. From the very first frame at second 0, Nora begins speaking immediately in a hushed, excited voice in three-quarter profile toward the lens. The Triceratops flares its nostrils and sniffs the air toward her.
timeline_action.3-7s: The Triceratops shifts its weight back onto its hind legs for a moment (anticipation), then takes two slow, heavy steps forward out from behind the fern clump into the open soil (reveal), stopping about two meters from the log. Each front foot plants and presses a visible print into the damp soil before the next foot lifts; its whole body rolls slightly from side to side with each step and settles when it stops.
timeline_action.7-10s: It lowers its head, closes its beak around one low fern frond at its feet, tears it off with a short sideways tug and chews, jaw working steadily. The tug and the first bites are finished by about second 9.5; the last half second is a quiet hold while it keeps chewing. Nora finishes her line toward the lens by about second 9.

The Triceratops stands behind the fern clump in the left midground, head raised, beak closed, not eating; its head, frill and front half show above the fronds; every frond in front of it is intact.
